---
title: "totalme"
subtitle: "The Total Marginal Effect for multiple-outcome models"
---
<<dd_version: 2>>

In a model with several outcome categories -- a multinomial or ordered logit, or
the probabilities of individual counts -- a predictor has one marginal effect per
category. `totalme` summarizes them in a single Total Marginal Effect: the total
amount of probability the predictor moves across the outcome categories, with a
standard error. The summary can be reported for one model, compared across
predictors, and compared across models or groups.

<!-- CHECK: definition sentence and the citation (Mize & Han 2025, Sociological
     Science). -->

## Installation

```stata
net install totalme, from("https://tdmize.github.io/data/totalme") replace
```

<!-- CHECK: install location. -->

## Basic use

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
sysuse nlsw88, clear
drop if missing(occupation)
recode occupation (1/2 = 1 "Professional/managerial") (3/5 = 2 "Sales/clerical/craft") ///
                  (6/13 = 3 "Other"), gen(occ3)

quietly mlogit occ3 i.collgrad c.age i.south, vce(robust)

totalme collgrad
<</dd_do>>
```

The Total Marginal Effect of a college degree is the total change in the
predicted distribution across the three occupation groups. `totalme` can also be
requested as an option of [`mecompare`](../mecompare/index.html), which places
the summary beneath the per-outcome marginal effects.
